_note: Config for tools/build-demo.mjs — apps/runner-macs with ?guest=1&School=…: the guest Portal branch. Run node demos/custom-forms/build.mjs (it runs build-logic.mjs, the template prep, then tools/build-demo.mjs on every build.*.json). src is the prep output: the app's pages/Index.html with ONLY the doGet branch for this surface kept and include_('pages/X') respelled include('pages/X') (see build.mjs); includeDir is the app root because the partials are named with their pages/ prefix. Demo-only edits, all at the page edges, none in the app's own scripts: (1) base target _top becomes _self so the page stays inside the switcher's frame, and DEMO_APP names the Apps Script project this page belongs to, ahead of the vendored server (logic.js); (2) every template output tag is answered by the app's OWN doGet — mock.js runs the vendored Router.js doGet(e) with this page's query string and captures what it assigns to the template (t.mode, t.formId, t.siteName ...) as DEMO_DOGET, so a quoted <?= x ?> becomes DEMO_DOGET.x and a raw <?!= x ?> JSON value becomes JSON.parse(DEMO_DOGET.x); (3) Theme.html's <?!= themeCss ?> is left as a comment and mock.js adds the CSS that this app's include_('pages/Theme') renders (ThemeLogic over the context's THEME_JSON), so MACS pages wear MACS's palette exactly as in production. When doGet's branch is a different surface (a ?form= link on the portal page, say), mock.js moves to that surface's page — the one template conditional a static page cannot carry.
replace:
<base target="_self">
  <script>var DEMO_APP = 'runner-macs', DEMO_SURFACE = 'macs-portal'; // demo: which Apps Script project and which doGet branch this page is</script>
  <script src="logic.js"></script>
/* themeCss: added at load by mock.js — what this app's include_('pages/Theme') renders */
location.href = portalUrl; // demo: stay inside the showcase frame
